subjects.name: Englisch
subjects.description: English is the first foreign language in almost all Länder. It usually starts in Kl. 3 (Kl. 1 in some Länder), becomes a core subject with explicit grammar from Kl. 5 and reaches about A2 by Kl. 7 and B1 (Gymnasium: B1+) at the MSA in Kl. 10. In the Gymnasiale Oberstufe it is taken as a Grundkurs (grundlegendes Niveau, gA) or Leistungskurs (erhöhtes Niveau, eA). The KMK Abitur standards (2012) set B2 and, for English, C1 in the receptive skills; literature, film and the societies of the English-speaking world become central.

sources.notes: Owned by gym-englisch; shared with the Französisch pass. Code = official section number + '.' + bullet index in document order within that section, counting every bullet of the section, gA bullets first and then eA bullets as they appear (e.g. 2.1.1.3 = third bullet of 2.1.1 Hör-/Hörsehverstehen; 2.3.2 = second bullet of 2.3 Text- und Medienkompetenz). Sections coded: 2.1.1 Hör-/Hörsehverstehen, 2.1.2 Leseverstehen, 2.1.3 Sprechen (one continuous count over 'An Gesprächen teilnehmen', bullets 1–9, and 'Zusammenhängendes monologisches Sprechen', bullets 10–16), 2.1.4 Schreiben, 2.1.5 Sprachmittlung, 2.1.6 Verfügen über sprachliche Mittel, 2.2 Interkulturelle kommunikative Kompetenz (no gA/eA split), 2.3 Text- und Medienkompetenz, 2.4 Sprachbewusstheit, 2.5 Sprachlernkompetenz. eA-only bullets are marked '(eA)' in the title; 'Englisch:' or 'Französisch:' marks language-specific wording. In 2.4 the official PDF prints one sentence over two bullet markers ('…Möglichkeiten ihrer Lösung,' / 'u. a. durch den Einsatz von Kompensationsstrategien abwägen'); both markers are counted, so 2.4.3 and 2.4.4 belong together. All bullets of section 2 are listed. Titles are short paraphrases, not official text.

sources.level: Ende Erprobungsstufe (Kl. 6, A1/A2), Ende erste Stufe (Kl. 8, A2 mit Anteilen B1), Ende zweite Stufe (Kl. 10, B1+)
sources.notes: The project built these codes; titles are short paraphrases. Scheme: <STUFE>.<AREA>.<n>. STUFE: E = Erprobungsstufe (Kl. 5–6), S1 = erste Stufe (in G9 Kl. 7–8), S2 = zweite Stufe (in G9 Kl. 9–10). AREA: GR = Grammatik and AI = Aussprache und Intonation, n = dash item of the 'Fachliche Konkretisierungen' column in document order; WS = Wortschatz and TMK = Text- und Medienkompetenz, n = competence-expectation bullet in document order; SOW = Soziokulturelles Orientierungswissen, n = dash item (Themenfeld) of its 'Fachliche Konkretisierungen' column (1 persönliche Lebensgestaltung, 2 Ausbildung/Schule, 3 Teilhabe am gesellschaftlichen Leben, 4 Berufsorientierung). Only codes cited by gym-englisch topics are listed. The plan does not name grades for the stages because it also served G8; the G9 mapping is the one used in NRW G9 schools.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Present Perfect vs Simple Past
topics.nameDe: Present Perfect und Simple Past im Vergleich
topics.description: Choose between the present perfect (a link to now: experiences, results, an unfinished period with since/for) and the simple past (a finished time in the past). German speakers find this contrast hard because the German Perfekt covers both.
evidence: Form the present perfect with have/has + past participle, including common irregular participles
Use since and for correctly with the present perfect ("I've lived here since 2019 / for five years")
Explain why "Yesterday I have seen…" is wrong and use the simple past with past time expressions
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} wants to say in English that they have known their best friend for five years, do they say "I have known her for five years" rather than "I know her since five years"?

prerequisites.reason: Needs past participles and the simple past forms it is contrasted with
Awareness that German and English tenses do not match one to one

osMatches.note: os is first-language (L1) English; here English as a foreign language (L2); the contrast with the German Perfekt is the focus

topics.laenderNotes: Introduced at the end of Kl. 6 in NRW (Erprobungsstufe) and Bayern (Jgst. 6, resultative use); the contrast with the simple past and the use of since/for are consolidated in Kl. 7.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Past Progressive and Past Perfect
topics.description: Tell past events with the right narrative tense: the past progressive for background and interrupted actions ("I was reading when the phone rang") and the past perfect for something that happened before another past event.
evidence: Combine past progressive and simple past with when/while to show an interrupted action
Use the past perfect to make clear which of two past events happened first
Retell a short story using simple past, past progressive and past perfect where each is needed
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} tells a story in English, can they say "When we arrived, the film had already started" to show what happened first?

prerequisites.reason: Narrative tenses are built around the simple past
The past perfect uses the past participle learned with the present perfect
Same be + -ing pattern as the past progressive
The German Plusquamperfekt is a familiar model for the past perfect

osMatches.note: os covers progressive tenses, not the past perfect

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern introduces the past progressive in Jgst. 6 and the past perfect in Jgst. 7; NRW lists both for the first stage of Sek I (Kl. 7–8).

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Talking about the Future
topics.nameDe: Zukunft ausdrücken: will-future, going to, present progressive
topics.description: Choose a suitable future form: will for predictions, spontaneous decisions and promises, going to for plans and predictions from present evidence, the present progressive for fixed arrangements and the simple present for timetables.
evidence: Use will for spontaneous decisions and offers ("I'll help you") and for predictions
Distinguish going to (intention) from the present progressive (fixed arrangement) when talking about their own plans
Use the simple present for timetabled events ("The train leaves at 8.15")
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English what they are doing next weekend and make a spontaneous offer like "I'll carry that for you"?

prerequisites.reason: Extends going to with will and other future forms
The present progressive is reused for arrangements
The simple present is reused for timetables

osMatches.note: os has one simple future; no choice between will, going to and present progressive

topics.laenderNotes: will-future and timetable future come in Kl. 6 in NRW and Bayern; NRW adds further ways of talking about the future in Kl. 7–8 and the future progressive and future perfect in Kl. 9–10.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Conditional Sentences Type I
topics.description: Talk about real, possible conditions and their likely results with if + simple present and will, can, must or an imperative in the main clause, and use when and unless correctly.
evidence: Form type I sentences with the simple present in the if-clause (no will after if)
Use unless correctly ("You'll miss the bus unless you hurry")
Use type I sentences to make promises, warnings and offers in a role play
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} say "If it rains, we will stay at home" rather than "If it will rain…"?

prerequisites.reason: The main clause uses the will-future
The if-clause uses the simple present

topics.laenderNotes: Taught at the end of Kl. 6 in NRW and Bayern and revised in Kl. 7 as the basis for types II and III.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Present Perfect Progressive
topics.description: Use the present perfect progressive for actions that began in the past and are still going on, or have just stopped with visible results, often with since and for ("I've been waiting for an hour").
evidence: Form the present perfect progressive with have/has been + -ing
Choose between present perfect simple (result, how many) and progressive (duration, activity)
Explain why stative verbs like know or own are not used in the progressive
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell a friend in English how long they have been learning English or playing their instrument?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the present perfect simple and since/for
Uses the progressive -ing form

osMatches.note: os progressive tenses without the perfect progressive

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 7; NRW first stage of Sek I (Kl. 7–8).

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Conditional Sentences Type II
topics.nameDe: if-Sätze Typ II (irreale Bedingungen der Gegenwart)
topics.description: Talk about unreal or unlikely situations in the present or future with if + simple past and would or could ("If I had more time, I would…"), including "If I were you…" for advice.

Give advice with "If I were you, I would…"
Explain the difference in meaning between "If I win…" and "If I won…"

The if-clause uses simple past forms

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Conditional Sentences Type III
topics.description: Speculate about the past and express regret with if + past perfect and would have + past participle, and recognise mixed conditionals that link a past condition to a present result.
evidence: Form type III sentences correctly ("If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the train")
Express regret about the past with type III and with "I wish I had…"
Identify the type of each conditional in a text and explain its meaning
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} say in English what would have happened if a historical event or a film's plot had gone differently?

prerequisites.reason: Extends unreal conditions to the past
The if-clause uses the past perfect

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern already teaches type III (with mixed forms) in Jgst. 7, NRW within the first stage (Kl. 7–8). Placed here after type II, from Kl. 8, with consolidation in Kl. 9.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Relative Clauses
topics.description: Add information about people and things with who, which, that and whose, leave out the relative pronoun in contact clauses, and separate non-defining relative clauses with commas.
evidence: Combine two sentences with who, which, that or whose
Recognise when the relative pronoun can be left out ("the book I read")
Punctuate a non-defining relative clause with commas and explain why that cannot be used there
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain an English word they cannot translate with a relative clause, such as "It's a person who…" or "It's a thing which…"?

prerequisites.reason: Relative clauses keep English subject–verb–object order
German relative clauses are the familiar model; English differs in pronoun choice and commas

osMatches.note: os is first-language (L1) English; here English as a foreign language (L2)

topics.laenderNotes: Defining relative clauses and contact clauses: Bayern Jgst. 6, NRW Kl. 7–8. Non-defining clauses and sentence-relative which: NRW Kl. 7–10, Bayern Jgst. 9.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Modal Verbs and Their Substitutes
topics.description: Express ability, permission, obligation, advice and possibility with modal verbs (can, may, must, should, might, ought to) and use their substitutes (be able to, be allowed to, have to) in other tenses. Avoid the German trap that mustn't does not mean 'muss nicht'.
evidence: Use be able to, be allowed to and have to in past and future forms
Explain the difference between mustn't (prohibition) and needn't / don't have to (no obligation)
Use might, could and may to express degrees of possibility
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that "You mustn't do it" means 'Du darfst es nicht tun' and not 'Du musst es nicht tun'?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on can as the first modal verb
Substitutes are needed in future forms (will be able to)
must not / muss nicht is a classic false friend

osMatches.note: os is first-language (L1) English; here English as a foreign language (L2); substitute forms and mustn't/needn't are added here

topics.laenderNotes: Substitute forms: Bayern Jgst. 6, NRW Kl. 7–8. might, ought to, would, used to: NRW Kl. 9–10; would and used to: Bayern Jgst. 9.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: The Passive
topics.description: Use the passive to focus on what happens rather than who does it, in different tenses and with modal verbs, add the agent with by only when it matters, and form the personal passive of verbs with two objects ("She was given a prize").
evidence: Form the passive in the simple present, simple past, present perfect and with modals ("can be recycled")
Turn an active news sentence into the passive and decide whether the by-agent is needed
Use the personal passive with give, send, offer and show ("I was offered a job")
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} describe in English how something is made or when a building was built, using passive sentences like "It was built in 1889"?

Passive forms with modal verbs

topics.name: Gerund and Infinitive
topics.description: Use the -ing form as a noun (gerund) as subject, after prepositions and after verbs such as enjoy, avoid and look forward to. Use the to-infinitive after verbs such as want and decide and in in order to, and know the verbs whose meaning changes (stop, remember, try).

evidence: Shorten relative clauses with present and past participles ("a book written in 1949")

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Style and Register for the Situation
topics.description: Reflect on how medium, addressee, purpose and register shape language, compare varieties and registers across languages, and deliberately adapt their own style, for example from an informal post to an academic essay.
evidence: Rewrite a text in a different register and explain each change (vocabulary, syntax, contractions, hedging)
Analyse how register signals the relationship between speakers in a literary or media text
Compare formality and politeness conventions in English and German and act on them
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} rewrite a chatty social-media post as a formal statement for a newspaper and explain what they changed?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on recognising varieties and Standard English
Formal letters were the first contrast between formal and informal style
Needs terms to describe style

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Understanding Authentic Audio
topics.description: Understand authentic and lightly adapted listening texts on familiar topics, such as radio reports, podcasts, interviews and announcements, for gist and detail, even when people speak at normal speed in a familiar variety.
evidence: Answer gist and detail questions about a 3–4 minute radio report or podcast
Note the key information from a station or airport announcement
Identify the speakers' opinions in a recorded conversation and whether they agree
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} listen to a short English podcast or radio item on a teenage topic and tell you what it was about and two details?

prerequisites.reason: Applies gist, selective and detailed listening to authentic texts

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Following Talks and Taking Notes
topics.description: Follow longer talks, presentations and explanations on familiar subjects, separate main points from supporting details, anticipate what comes next and take structured notes while listening.
evidence: Take notes on a 5-minute talk with key words and abbreviations and reconstruct its main points from them
Distinguish main points from examples and details in a presentation
Revise their expectations as a talk develops and say what they had predicted
topics.assessmentPrompt: After watching a short English talk (for example a TED-Ed video), can {{name}} use their notes to explain its main points?

prerequisites.reason: Needs secure understanding of authentic speech
Knowing how presentations are built helps to follow them

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Understanding Feature Films and Series
topics.description: Follow an English feature film or series episode, with or without subtitles, understand plot, characters and their relationships, and use images, music and context to fill gaps in understanding.
evidence: Summarise the plot of a film or episode and describe the relationships between the main characters
Explain how the images and music of a scene help them understand what is not said
Decide when English subtitles help and use them selectively
topics.assessmentPrompt: After watching an English film or series episode, can {{name}} tell you the story and what the main characters are like?

prerequisites.reason: Extends understanding of short videos to full-length films
Films use authentic, fast speech

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern lists film extracts (with subtitles if needed) in Jgst. 10; NRW lists audio and video clips in Kl. 7–10 and extracts from a feature film and a TV series in the Oberstufe.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Understanding Authentic Broadcasts
topics.nameDe: Authentische Hör- und Hörsehtexte verstehen (Nachrichten, Podcasts, Dokumentationen)
topics.description: Understand authentic news broadcasts, podcasts, documentaries and discussions on social and political topics, combine what is said with background knowledge, and grasp the speakers' moods and attitudes.
evidence: Extract the main points or specific details from an authentic news item or podcast, as the task requires
Identify the attitude of speakers in a discussion and the evidence for it (tone, word choice)
Relate what is said to the images and cultural context in a documentary extract
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} follow a BBC or NPR news report on a current issue and explain the main points and the speakers' positions?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on following longer talks
Audiovisual comprehension of longer texts

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Implicit Meaning and Challenging Speech
topics.nameDe: Implizites erschließen; schnelles und nicht-standardsprachliches Sprechen verstehen
topics.description: Understand complex listening and viewing texts on less familiar topics even when speech is fast, non-standard or disturbed by background noise, and interpret implicit information, attitudes and relationships between speakers.
evidence: Explain irony, understatement or hidden criticism in an interview or film scene
Follow speakers with strong regional accents or slang in an authentic recording
Infer the relationship between speakers from tone and from what is left unsaid
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} catch irony or hidden criticism in an English talk show or drama, even when people speak fast?

prerequisites.reason: Extends authentic listening to implicit meaning and harder conditions
Non-standard speech requires knowledge of varieties

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Reading Factual Texts
topics.description: Read longer factual texts on familiar topics (articles, websites, brochures), find the main points and specific details, work out unknown words from word parts and context, and combine information from several texts for a task.
evidence: Mark key sentences and write a heading for each paragraph of an article
Work out unknown words from prefixes, suffixes and context and check them
Collect information from two or three texts or websites to complete a task
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} read a one-page English article for teenagers and tell you its main points without translating every word?

prerequisites.reason: Extends skimming and scanning to longer factual texts
Inferring word meanings
The same strategies for non-fiction are practised in German

osMatches.note: os is first-language (L1) English; here English as a foreign language (L2)

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Reading a Young Adult Novel
topics.description: Read a whole graded reader or young adult novel in English, keep track of plot, characters and their relationships across a longer text, and respond personally to the story.
evidence: Keep a reading log with a short summary and a personal reaction for each chapter
Describe the main characters' traits and feelings with evidence from the text
Predict how the story will continue and compare this with what happens
topics.assessmentPrompt: Has {{name}} read a whole book in English, and can they tell you what it is about and what they think of the main character?

prerequisites.reason: Extends reading simple stories to a whole book
Novels are narrated in past tenses

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern mentions readers (Lektüren) in Jgst. 9 and requires a novel as a whole text in Jgst. 10; NRW lists a longer narrative text for Kl. 9–10.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Reading Complex Authentic Texts
topics.description: Read authentic texts of different types and periods on abstract topics, select texts and passages for a purpose, apply reading strategies independently and recognise implicit as well as explicit statements.
evidence: Identify the main argument and supporting details of a newspaper feature or essay
Recognise implicit statements, such as what an author suggests without saying it
Choose suitable texts or passages from a dossier for a given research question
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} read an article from The Guardian or The New York Times on a social issue and explain both what it says and what it implies?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on reading factual texts for gist and detail
Stamina for longer texts

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Questioning Stereotypes
topics.description: Recognise stereotypes and clichés about English-speaking countries and about Germans, explain where they come from and question them with information from texts and personal encounters.
evidence: Collect common stereotypes about Britain, the USA and Germany and check them against facts
Explain how media and jokes reinforce stereotypes
Describe a situation in which a first impression of another culture turned out to be wrong
topics.assessmentPrompt: If someone says 'All Americans eat fast food', can {{name}} explain in English why that is a stereotype?

prerequisites.reason: Needs first knowledge of life in Britain to compare with clichés
Openness towards other languages and cultures

osMatches.note: os is about stereotypes of social groups in general; here national and cultural stereotypes

topics.laenderNotes: NRW names explaining and questioning stereotypes as a Kl. 7–8 expectation; Bayern addresses stereotypes explicitly in Jgst. 10.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Intercultural Encounters and Misunderstandings
topics.description: Act appropriately when meeting people from English-speaking cultures, for example on an exchange: notice different conventions (politeness, directness, small talk, personal space, punctuality) and recognise and clear up simple misunderstandings.
evidence: Explain why British indirectness ("That's quite interesting") can be misread by Germans
Use small talk and polite softeners appropriately when meeting a host family
Analyse a case of intercultural misunderstanding and suggest how to resolve it
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know why a direct German 'No, that's wrong' can sound rude in English, and how to say it more politely?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on basic politeness conventions
Conventions must be told apart from stereotypes
Encounters happen in everyday situations

osMatches.note: os covers non-verbal signals only

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Changing Perspectives and Weighing Values
topics.description: Take the perspective of people from other cultures in texts and encounters, compare and weigh different viewpoints, question their own prejudices, and assess values and attitudes against international conventions such as human rights.
evidence: Describe an issue (e.g. gun laws, the monarchy) from the perspective of different groups in the target culture
Identify their own culturally shaped assumptions in a first reaction to a text and revise them
Evaluate a practice or statement with reference to human rights rather than personal taste
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why many Americans defend the right to bear arms, even if they themselves disagree, and judge the debate with good arguments?

prerequisites.reason: Questioning stereotypes is the first step towards a change of perspective
Experience of intercultural encounters

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Communicating in English as a Lingua Franca
topics.nameDe: Englisch als lingua franca: Missverständnisse erkennen und klären
topics.description: Communicate in English with speakers of many first languages, observe conventions of distance and closeness, recognise and resolve misunderstandings and conflicts caused by language or culture, and reflect on the effect of their own language behaviour.
evidence: Adjust their English for non-native partners (clear structure, few idioms) in an international exchange
Identify the cause of a misunderstanding in a lingua franca conversation and repair it
Reflect on how their tone and directness came across in an international online project
topics.assessmentPrompt: In an international online project, can {{name}} work with partners from different countries in English and sort out misunderstandings politely?

prerequisites.reason: Extends intercultural conventions to lingua franca settings
Awareness of many Englishes

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: The Four Nations of the UK
topics.description: Know the four nations of the UK (England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland): their geography, capitals, languages, symbols and some regional identities, and the difference between England, Great Britain and the United Kingdom.
evidence: Explain the difference between England, Great Britain, the United Kingdom and the British Isles
Name the capitals, flags and national symbols of the four nations and locate them on a map
Describe one region (e.g. Wales or Scotland) and its language or culture in a short presentation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain why a Scot might not like being called 'English'?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on first knowledge of everyday life in Britain
Locating the UK among the countries of Europe

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Wales and the South West as tourist regions in Jgst. 7, Scotland's history and politics in Jgst. 10. NRW: a region of Great Britain in Kl. 5–6, life in the UK in Kl. 7–8.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Teenage Life and School in the USA
topics.nameDe: Leben Jugendlicher und Schulalltag in den USA
topics.description: Know about the everyday life of young people in the USA (high school, grades, sports and clubs, food, festivals such as Thanksgiving and the Fourth of July) and compare it with life in Germany.
evidence: Describe a typical US high school day and compare it with their own school
Explain the origins and customs of Thanksgiving and Independence Day
Name some states and regions of the USA and find them on a map
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English how an American high school differs from their own school?

prerequisites.reason: Extends the overview of English-speaking countries to the USA
Information comes from factual texts

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: The Founding of the USA
topics.nameDe: Die Gründung der USA: Pilgerväter, Unabhängigkeit, Native Americans
topics.description: Know key steps in the early history of the USA (the Pilgrim Fathers and New England, the Boston Tea Party, the Declaration of Independence, westward expansion) and their impact on Native Americans.
evidence: Put key events from 1620 to the late 19th century in order on a timeline
Explain the main ideas of the Declaration of Independence in simple English
Describe the consequences of westward expansion for Native American peoples
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} tell you in English why the Fourth of July is celebrated and what westward expansion meant for Native Americans?

prerequisites.reason: Festivals like Thanksgiving lead into the history
Working with timelines

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: American Revolution and Declaration of Independence
externalPrerequisites.reason: Often taught in Geschichte around the same time

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: colonisation of North America in Jgst. 7, founding of the USA and the West in Jgst. 8. NRW: historically important people and events of the UK and USA in Kl. 7–8.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Political Systems of the UK and the USA
topics.nameDe: Politische Systeme Großbritanniens und der USA (Grundlagen)
topics.description: Understand the basics of the UK's constitutional monarchy and parliamentary system and of the US presidential system, compare them with Germany and follow news about elections.
evidence: Explain the roles of the monarch, the Prime Minister and Parliament in the UK
Explain the roles of the President, Congress and the Supreme Court and the separation of powers in the USA
Compare one feature of each system with Germany (e.g. how the head of government is chosen)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English the difference between the British Prime Minister and the American President?

prerequisites.reason: The US system grows out of the founding of the USA
The UK's structure as a union of nations
Basic principles of elections

externalPrerequisites.subject: Politik und Wirtschaft
externalPrerequisites.concept: parliamentary democracy and separation of powers in Germany
externalPrerequisites.reason: The German system is the point of comparison

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 8 (constitutional monarchy, presidential system); NRW Kl. 7–10 (political aspects of life in the UK and USA).

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: African American History and Civil Rights
topics.description: Know the history of African Americans from slavery and the Civil War to segregation and the Civil Rights Movement (Rosa Parks, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X), and its legacy today, for example Black Lives Matter.
evidence: Put the key stages from slavery to the Civil Rights Act on a timeline
Present the ideas and methods of a civil rights leader (e.g. King's 'I Have a Dream' speech)
Relate a current debate about racism in the USA to this history
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English who Rosa Parks was and why the bus boycott mattered?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the early history of the USA
Racism is linked to stereotypes and prejudice

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 10 (slavery, Civil War, Civil Rights Movement); elsewhere often in Kl. 9–10 or within the Oberstufe topic 'American Dream'.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Australia and Its Indigenous Peoples
topics.description: Get to know another English-speaking country in depth, typically Australia: its geography, colonial history, multicultural society and the situation of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, including the Stolen Generations.
evidence: Describe Australia's geography and how it shapes where people live
Explain the consequences of British colonisation for Aboriginal peoples, including the Stolen Generations
Compare life in Australia (or Canada or New Zealand) with life in Germany in a short presentation
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English what the 'Stolen Generations' were?

prerequisites.reason: Extends the overview of English-speaking countries
Information comes from factual texts

osMatches.note: os (Australian History) covers the impact of British contact on First Nations peoples only

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: Australia (with New Zealand) in Jgst. 9 and Canada in Jgst. 8; NRW requires 'a further anglophone country' of the school's choice in Kl. 9–10.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Growing Up: Identity and Diversity
topics.description: Discuss how young people in English-speaking societies develop their identity between conformity and individualism, and how ethnic, cultural, social, sexual and gender diversity shape their opportunities and challenges, often through young adult fiction.
evidence: Analyse how a young adult novel or film presents a character's search for identity
Discuss pressures of conformity and peer groups with examples from texts
Present facts and views on diversity and discrimination among young people in the UK or USA
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} discuss in English how a character in a young adult novel struggles to find out who they are?

prerequisites.reason: Young adult novels are the typical material
Diversity and discrimination build on questioning stereotypes

topics.laenderNotes: NRW Einführungsphase topic ('Das Individuum und die Gesellschaft im Wandel', identity in young adult fiction).

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Studying and Working Abroad
topics.nameDe: Lernen, Leben und Arbeiten im englischsprachigen Ausland
topics.description: Explore options for spending time abroad after school (exchange, gap year, work and travel, university in the UK or USA), compare education systems and use English as a lingua franca for work and study.
evidence: Compare the costs, requirements and benefits of two programmes abroad
Explain how applying to university works in the UK or USA compared with Germany
Write or present a personal statement for a programme abroad
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} explain in English what a gap year or a college application in the USA involves?

prerequisites.reason: Applications and CVs are reused for programmes abroad
First knowledge of the US school system

topics.laenderNotes: NRW Einführungsphase ('Lernen, Leben und Arbeiten im englischsprachigen Ausland'); Bayern treats UK/US education and the world of work in Jgst. 9.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: The American Dream
topics.nameDe: Der amerikanische Traum: Ideale und Wirklichkeit
topics.description: Understand the American Dream as a founding myth (freedom, equality, pursuit of happiness, upward mobility), trace it from the Declaration of Independence and immigration history to today, and judge it against social realities such as inequality and racism.
evidence: Explain the ideals of the American Dream with reference to key texts (Declaration of Independence, speeches)
Analyse how a novel, film or song presents the Dream or its failure
Assess whether the American Dream is still achievable today, using statistics and examples
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain what the American Dream means and argue in English whether it is still alive?

prerequisites.reason: The Dream is rooted in the founding of the USA
Racism is a central counterpoint to the Dream

topics.laenderNotes: A long-standing Abitur topic in many Länder (NRW: 'Amerikanische Ideale und Realitäten'; Bayern 12/13: American Dream in the context of immigration).

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: US Politics and a Divided Society
topics.nameDe: Politik und Gesellschaft der USA (Verfassung, Wahlen, Polarisierung)
topics.description: Understand the US Constitution and checks and balances, how presidential elections work, the role of the USA in the world and current conflicts in a polarised society (e.g. gun control, immigration, the role of religion).
evidence: Explain the Electoral College and the separation of powers
Analyse a current political conflict in the USA from at least two perspectives
Discuss the global role of the USA, for example in its relations with Europe
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English how the US president is elected and why American politics is so polarised?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the basics of the presidential system
Political conflicts often turn on American ideals

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: British Politics and Brexit
topics.nameDe: Politisches System des UK und Brexit
topics.description: Understand Westminster democracy (Parliament, government, monarchy, first-past-the-post), devolution to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, and the UK's changing relationship with Europe, especially Brexit and its consequences.
evidence: Explain how a UK general election and the first-past-the-post system work
Describe devolution and the debate on Scottish independence
Present the arguments of both sides of the Brexit debate and some of its consequences
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English why the UK left the EU and what that means for young people?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the basics of the British system
Devolution concerns the four nations
Basic knowledge of the EU

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Britain between Tradition and Change
topics.description: Discuss British society today between tradition and change: the monarchy, class and education, and multicultural Britain shaped by immigration from the Commonwealth.
evidence: Discuss arguments for and against the monarchy today
Explain how class and education (state and public schools, Oxbridge) shape opportunities
Describe the experience of a migrant community (e.g. the Windrush generation) and its place in British identity
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English what 'multicultural Britain' means, using an example such as the Windrush generation?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on knowledge of the UK
Immigration from the Commonwealth follows from the Empire

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: The British Empire and the Commonwealth
topics.description: Know how the British Empire rose and declined (first and second Empire, decolonisation) and what the Commonwealth of Nations is today, and judge the legacy of colonialism from different perspectives.
evidence: Outline the main stages of the British Empire and of decolonisation on a timeline and map
Explain what the Commonwealth is and how it differs from the Empire
Compare British and formerly colonised perspectives on the Empire's legacy
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English how the British Empire became the Commonwealth and why its legacy is controversial?

prerequisites.reason: A first case study of colonisation
Knowledge of the UK itself

externalPrerequisites.subject: Geschichte
externalPrerequisites.concept: European imperialism and colonialism in the 19th century

osMatches.note: os covers British colonies in Australia only

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern Jgst. 11 (colonisation, First and Second Empire, Commonwealth); NRW Qualifikationsphase (national self-image and colonial legacy).

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Post-Colonial Societies
topics.nameDe: Postkoloniale Lebenswirklichkeiten (z. B. Indien, Nigeria, Südafrika)
topics.description: Study one post-colonial English-speaking society in depth (e.g. India, Nigeria, South Africa or Canada): its history under British rule, independence, the role of English today and current social issues, using non-fiction and literature from that country.
evidence: Explain how British rule and independence shaped the country's society and language situation
Analyse a text or film by an author from that country that deals with the colonial legacy
Discuss a current issue (e.g. caste, the legacy of apartheid, multilingualism) from local perspectives
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English what life in post-colonial India or South Africa is like and how the colonial past still matters?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on the history of the Empire
Requires taking non-British perspectives

topics.laenderNotes: NRW: 'a further English-speaking culture' in the Qualifikationsphase, with the legacy of British rule as an extra Leistungskurs focus; Bayern: post-colonial developments in Canada, India and South Africa in Jgst. 11.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Globalisation: Opportunities and Risks
topics.description: Discuss economic, social and cultural globalisation (global trade, outsourcing, the global job market, migration, cultural homogenisation) and its winners and losers, with examples from the English-speaking world.
evidence: Explain key terms (outsourcing, global supply chain, brain drain) with examples
Analyse statistics or cartoons on global inequality or migration
Weigh the opportunities and risks of globalisation for young people in a comment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} discuss in English whether globalisation does more good than harm, with examples?

prerequisites.reason: Personal mobility is one side of globalisation
Material comes from complex authentic texts

externalPrerequisites.subject: Erdkunde
externalPrerequisites.concept: economic globalisation and global trade networks

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern treats industrialisation, globalisation and digitalisation in Jgst. 11.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Environment and Sustainability
topics.description: Discuss climate change, environmental protection and sustainable lifestyles in English, using authentic texts, speeches and data from the English-speaking world, and judge individual and political responses.
evidence: Explain the causes and consequences of climate change with suitable vocabulary
Analyse a speech or campaign by a climate activist or politician
Propose and evaluate measures for a more sustainable school or town
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English what young people can do against climate change and argue which measures really help?

prerequisites.reason: Information comes from factual texts
Measures are debated

externalPrerequisites.subject: Erdkunde
externalPrerequisites.concept: causes and consequences of climate change
externalPrerequisites.reason: Scientific background from Erdkunde and the sciences

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Media, Journalism and Social Media
topics.nameDe: Medien: Journalismus, soziale Medien und Manipulation
topics.description: Discuss the role of the media in English-speaking societies: quality press and tabloids, journalism between information and entertainment, and social media and digital platforms between participation and manipulation (filter bubbles, fake news).
evidence: Compare how a quality paper and a tabloid report the same event
Explain how algorithms and filter bubbles shape what users see
Evaluate measures against disinformation in a discussion or comment
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} explain in English how social media can be used to manipulate opinions, and how to protect yourself?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on analysing journalistic texts
Persuasive techniques in the media
Basic idea of fake news and manipulated images

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Science, Technology and Ethics
topics.nameDe: Wissenschaft, Technik und Ethik (z. B. KI, Gentechnik)
topics.description: Discuss scientific and technological progress (artificial intelligence, genetic engineering, surveillance) as an opportunity and a challenge for society, using non-fiction texts and science fiction, and evaluate ethical arguments.
evidence: Explain a current technology and the ethical questions it raises
Analyse how a non-fiction text or film presents the risks and benefits of a technology
Argue an ethical position in a debate, distinguishing facts from values
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} discuss in English whether artificial intelligence should be allowed to make decisions about people?

prerequisites.reason: Science fiction and dystopias dramatise these questions
Material comes from complex non-fiction
Basic idea of the limits and risks of AI

topics.laenderNotes: NRW's 2014 plan made 'Fortschritt und Ethik' a Leistungskurs topic; the 2023 plan includes scientific and technical progress for both course levels, as does Bayern 12/13 (gA).

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Writing Structured Paragraphs
topics.nameDe: Strukturierte Absätze schreiben (topic sentence, linking words)
topics.description: Organise their own texts in paragraphs with a topic sentence, supporting sentences and examples, and connect ideas with linking words (first, however, therefore, in addition).
evidence: Write a paragraph with a clear topic sentence and two supporting details
Use linking words for addition, contrast, cause and consequence
Plan a text with an outline before writing and divide it into paragraphs
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes half a page in English, is it divided into paragraphs that each have one main idea?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on writing simple connected texts
Planning and revising

osMatches.note: os is first-language (L1) English; here English as a foreign language (L2)

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Writing Stories and Diary Entries
topics.description: Write narrative texts such as stories, diary entries and story continuations, using narrative tenses, direct speech and descriptive language to make events and feelings vivid, also from a changed perspective.
evidence: Write a story of about 250 words with a clear beginning, climax and ending
Use past tenses correctly, including the past perfect for earlier events, and punctuate direct speech
Continue a textbook story or rewrite it from another character's point of view
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write a short English story with a beginning, a turning point and an ending, using past tenses correctly?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on writing connected texts
Stories need the narrative tenses
Narrative techniques from German writing lessons

osMatches.note: os is first-language (L1) English; here English as a foreign language (L2)

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Writing Reports and Articles
topics.description: Write factual reports and articles for a school magazine or blog, with a headline, an opening that answers the key questions, and a neutral, well-ordered account of facts and reasons.
evidence: Write a report about a school event that answers who, what, when, where and why
Use a headline and a lead paragraph that make readers want to read on
Keep facts and opinions apart and give reasons for what happened
topics.assessmentPrompt: Can {{name}} write a short English article for a school magazine about a trip or event, with a headline and the key facts first?

prerequisites.reason: Reports need clear paragraphs
Model texts come from reading articles
Report writing is practised in German

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Writing Formal Letters and Emails
topics.description: Write formal letters and emails (enquiry, request, complaint) with the right layout, salutation and closing, a polite formal register and a clear statement of purpose.
evidence: Use suitable openings and closings (Dear Sir or Madam … Yours faithfully; Dear Ms Smith … Yours sincerely)
Write an enquiry to a language school or hostel asking for specific information
Avoid contractions and informal words and use polite forms (I would be grateful if…)
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could {{name}} write a polite formal email in English to a hostel to ask about prices and free rooms?

prerequisites.reason: Moves from informal messages to formal correspondence
Polite requests use could and would
The body of the letter is structured in paragraphs

osMatches.note: os lists formal letters among many genres

topics.laenderNotes: Formal letters and formal vs informal vocabulary in Bayern Jgst. 8; NRW lists formal letters and emails as target texts in Kl. 9–10.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Writing a CV and Letter of Application

osMatches.note: os dictionary use for spelling only

topics.laenderNotes: Many Länder allow dictionaries in the written English Abitur, so their efficient use is trained from Sek I.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Using Translation and AI Tools Critically
topics.nameDe: Maschinelle Übersetzung und KI-Werkzeuge kritisch nutzen
topics.description: Use machine translation, AI writing assistants and grammar checkers as learning aids, check their output for errors in meaning, register and context, and know the rules on when such tools are allowed.
evidence: Compare a machine translation with the original and find errors in meaning or register
Use an AI tool to get feedback on their own text and decide which suggestions to accept
Explain when using such tools supports learning and when it replaces their own work
topics.assessmentPrompt: If {{name}} uses a translation app or AI tool for English homework, can they spot where it got the meaning or tone wrong?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on first use of translators and apps
Basic idea of the limits and risks of AI

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Directing Own Language Learning
topics.description: Assess their own English against CEFR B2/C1 descriptors, document progress, set goals and choose strategies and resources (media, reading, exchanges, online forums) to keep improving beyond the classroom.
evidence: Self-assess their skills with CEFR descriptors and compare the result with teacher feedback
Plan and carry out a personal learning project (e.g. reading a series, a podcast routine) with goals
Use authentic media and encounters outside school deliberately to extend their English
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} have a plan for improving their English outside school, for example through books, podcasts or series in English, and know where they need to improve?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on self-assessment with a language portfolio
Independent use of reference tools

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: British and American English
topics.description: Know the main differences in vocabulary, spelling and pronunciation between British and American English (flat/apartment, colour/color, the American r) and stay consistent in their own writing.
evidence: Give the American equivalents of at least 15 everyday British words (lift/elevator, holiday/vacation…)
Recognise and apply typical spelling differences (-our/-or, -re/-er, -ise/-ize)
Tell whether a speaker is British or American from pronunciation features
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} know that a Londoner's 'flat' is an 'apartment' in New York and that 'colour' is spelled 'color' there?

prerequisites.reason: British English is the variety met first in textbooks
Spelling differences build on basic English spelling

topics.laenderNotes: NRW: basic lexical and grammatical differences in Kl. 7–8; Bayern: Jgst. 8.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Collocations and Phrasal Verbs
topics.nameDe: Kollokationen, phrasal verbs und idiomatische Wendungen
topics.description: Learn words in their typical combinations (make a decision, heavy rain, take part in) and common phrasal verbs (give up, look after, find out), and use them instead of literal translations from German.
evidence: Use at least 20 common phrasal verbs correctly in context
Correct typical miscollocations from German ("make a photo" → take a photo)
Record new vocabulary as collocations or example sentences rather than single words
topics.assessmentPrompt: Does {{name}} say "take a photo" and "make a decision" in English, rather than translating word for word from German?

prerequisites.reason: Extends vocabulary-learning strategies to word combinations
Literal translation errors are the same trap as false friends

osMatches.note: os idioms for L1 readers; collocations and phrasal verbs are an L2 issue

topics.laenderNotes: Bayern: collocations and verbs with prepositions in Jgst. 8, basic phrasal verbs and idioms in Jgst. 10.

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Vocabulary for Analysis and Argument
topics.description: Use the functional vocabulary needed to discuss texts and issues in English: terms for text types and stylistic devices, verbs that describe what an author does (criticise, imply, emphasise) and connectives for argument.
evidence: Describe what an author does with precise verbs (states, suggests, ridicules, appeals to)
Use technical terms (narrator, metaphor, alliteration, tone, bias) correctly in an analysis
Link arguments with a range of connectives (furthermore, nevertheless, consequently, whereas)
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} writes about a text in English, do they use precise words like "the author criticises" or "the metaphor suggests" instead of "the author says"?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on learning words in combinations
First connectives for argument
First technical terms for narrative texts

topics.subject: Englisch
topics.name: Weak Forms and Connected Speech
topics.description: Understand and use features of natural spoken English: weak forms of small words (/ə/ in to, of, can), linking between words (linking r, an apple), contractions and unstressed syllables. Their speech sounds more fluent and fast speech becomes easier to follow.
evidence: Pronounce the weak form in "I can swim" /kən/ and the strong form in "Yes, I can" /kæn/
Link words smoothly ("far away" with linking r, "an orange")
Write down a short fast-spoken sentence and identify the reduced words
topics.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} reads an English sentence aloud, does it sound connected and natural rather than word by word?

prerequisites.reason: Builds on sentence stress and intonation
Weak forms are shown in phonetic transcription

topics.laenderNotes: NRW lists vowels in unstressed syllables and linking r for Kl. 7–8.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to understand authentic English audio such as radio reports, podcasts, interviews and announcements, for the gist and for details.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, authentische englische Hörtexte wie Radiobeiträge, Podcasts, Interviews und Durchsagen global und im Detail zu verstehen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to follow longer talks while taking notes and to understand whole English films and series episodes.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, längeren Vorträgen mit Notizen zu folgen und ganze englische Spielfilme und Serienfolgen zu verstehen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to understand authentic news, podcasts and documentaries, including the speakers' attitudes; in the Leistungskurs also irony, fast speech and strong accents.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, authentische Nachrichten, Podcasts und Dokumentationen samt den Haltungen der Sprechenden zu verstehen; im Leistungskurs auch Ironie, schnelles Sprechen und starke Akzente.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to manage travel and everyday situations in English, to discuss and justify opinions, and to give presentations from notes.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Reise- und Alltagssituationen auf Englisch zu bewältigen, Meinungen zu begründen und Referate frei mit Stichwortzetteln zu halten.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to take part in formal debates and to present and discuss a text or picture in an oral exam; in the Leistungskurs also to speak spontaneously on unfamiliar topics.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, sich an formellen Debatten zu beteiligen und in der mündlichen Prüfung einen Text oder ein Bild vorzustellen und zu diskutieren; im Leistungskurs auch spontan zu weniger vertrauten Themen zu sprechen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to read longer factual texts without translating every word and to read a whole young adult novel in English.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, längere Sachtexte zu verstehen, ohne jedes Wort zu übersetzen, und einen ganzen Jugendroman auf Englisch zu lesen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to read complex authentic texts such as newspaper features and essays and to recognise what they imply as well as what they say.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, komplexe authentische Texte wie Zeitungsreportagen und Essays zu erschließen und auch Unausgesprochenes zu erkennen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to write well-structured paragraphs, stories, diary entries, reports and formal emails in English.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, gut gegliederte Absätze, Geschichten, Tagebucheinträge, Berichte und formelle E-Mails auf Englisch zu schreiben.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to write argumentative texts, letters of application with a CV, and summaries of texts in their own words.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, argumentative Texte, Bewerbungen mit Lebenslauf und Zusammenfassungen von Texten in eigenen Worten zu schreiben.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning the Abitur writing tasks: understanding operators, writing text analyses, comments and creative texts based on a source; in the Leistungskurs also adapting texts for new audiences.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Schreibaufgaben des Abiturs: Operatoren verstehen, Textanalysen, Kommentare und kreative Texte zu einer Vorlage schreiben; im Leistungskurs auch Texte für neue Zielgruppen umgestalten.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to help people communicate across German and English, in conversations and by passing on the content of German texts in English.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, zwischen Deutsch und Englisch zu vermitteln, im Gespräch und indem es den Inhalt deutscher Texte auf Englisch wiedergibt.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to mediate complex German texts into English for a given reader and purpose, as in the Abitur; in the Leistungskurs also to add cultural explanations.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, komplexe deutsche Texte wie im Abitur adressaten- und zweckgerecht ins Englische zu mitteln; im Leistungskurs auch mit kulturellen Erläuterungen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the differences between British and American English and to use collocations and phrasal verbs instead of word-for-word translations.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Unterschiede zwischen britischem und amerikanischem Englisch und verwendet Kollokationen und phrasal verbs statt Wort-für-Wort-Übersetzungen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning the vocabulary needed to analyse texts and argue precisely in English.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt den Wortschatz, um auf Englisch Texte präzise zu analysieren und zu argumentieren.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning the core grammar of English: the present perfect and other tenses, future forms, conditional sentences, relative clauses, modal verbs, the passive, reported speech and the gerund.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Kerngrammatik des Englischen: present perfect und weitere Zeiten, Zukunftsformen, if-Sätze, Relativsätze, Modalverben, Passiv, indirekte Rede und Gerundium.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning participle constructions, to see English tenses as a system and to reflect on varieties of English around the world.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt Partizipialkonstruktionen, versteht die englischen Zeiten als System und denkt über Varietäten des Englischen weltweit nach.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to vary sentences and add emphasis in writing; in the Leistungskurs also to adapt style and register deliberately to the situation.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Sätze abwechslungsreich zu bauen und gezielt zu betonen; im Leistungskurs auch Stil und Register bewusst an die Situation anzupassen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to sound more natural in English by using weak forms and linking words together.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, natürlicher Englisch zu sprechen, indem es schwache Formen nutzt und Wörter miteinander verbindet.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to question stereotypes and to behave appropriately in encounters with people from English-speaking cultures, for example on an exchange.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Stereotype zu hinterfragen und sich in Begegnungen mit Menschen aus englischsprachigen Kulturen, etwa beim Austausch, angemessen zu verhalten.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to see issues from other cultures' perspectives, to weigh values against human rights and to communicate in English with people from all over the world.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Themen aus der Sicht anderer Kulturen zu betrachten, Werte an den Menschenrechten zu messen und auf Englisch mit Menschen aus aller Welt zu kommunizieren.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about the four nations of the UK, teenage life and the early history of the USA, and the political systems of Britain and America.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Landesteile des Vereinigten Königreichs, das Leben Jugendlicher und die Gründungsgeschichte der USA sowie die politischen Systeme Großbritanniens und der USA kennen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning about African American history and the Civil Rights Movement and about another English-speaking country such as Australia.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt die Geschichte der Afroamerikaner und die Bürgerrechtsbewegung sowie ein weiteres englischsprachiges Land wie Australien kennen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is studying the big Oberstufe topics: the American Dream, US and British politics and society, the Empire and post-colonial societies, globalisation, the environment, the media and the ethics of technology.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind beschäftigt sich mit den großen Oberstufenthemen: American Dream, Politik und Gesellschaft der USA und Großbritanniens, Empire und postkoloniale Gesellschaften, Globalisierung, Umwelt, Medien und Ethik der Technik.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to analyse English short stories: plot, characters and who tells the story.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, englische Kurzgeschichten zu analysieren: Handlung, Figuren und Erzählperspektive.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to write characterisations, understand poems and songs, analyse adverts, and describe pictures, cartoons and charts in English.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Charakterisierungen zu schreiben, Gedichte und Songs zu verstehen, Werbung zu analysieren und Bilder, Cartoons und Diagramme auf Englisch zu beschreiben.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to analyse novels, poems, plays, films, newspaper articles, speeches, cartoons and dystopian fiction, and meets Shakespeare; in the Leistungskurs they interpret a whole Shakespeare play and texts in their historical context.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Romane, Gedichte, Dramen, Filme, Zeitungsartikel, Reden, Cartoons und Dystopien zu analysieren, und lernt Shakespeare kennen; im Leistungskurs deutet es ein ganzes Shakespeare-Drama und Texte im historischen Kontext.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to use monolingual and online dictionaries well, checking meaning, collocations and register.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, ein- und zweisprachige Wörterbücher und Online-Wörterbücher gezielt zu nutzen und dabei Bedeutung, Kollokationen und Register zu prüfen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your child is learning to use translation apps and AI tools critically, spotting their errors instead of copying their output.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, Übersetzungs-Apps und KI-Werkzeuge kritisch zu nutzen und ihre Fehler zu erkennen, statt Ergebnisse einfach zu übernehmen.

clusters.subject: Englisch
clusters.summary: Your teenager is learning to assess their own English against B2/C1 and to plan how to keep improving through media and contacts outside school.
clusters.summaryDe: Ihr Kind lernt, das eigene Englisch am Niveau B2/C1 einzuschätzen und das Weiterlernen mit Medien und Kontakten außerhalb der Schule zu planen.
